title: The 60-second self intro
prompt:
Goal: Say 5–6 clean SVO sentences about yourself without freezing.

Record yourself: name, city, university + semester, what you study, one hobby. Full sentences only.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Describe your room (SVO only)
prompt:
Goal: Force English word order (verb second, not last).

90 seconds describing your hostel room. Every sentence must be Subject–Verb–Object. If you catch yourself putting the verb last, keep going — do not stop.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The a/an read-aloud
prompt:
Goal: Make a/an automatic before vowel and consonant sounds.

Write 10 sentences, each using a or an correctly (include: honest man, university, hour, orange, European client). Then read all 10 aloud and record.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Back-translation sprint
prompt:
Goal: Expose where Urdu word order breaks your English.

Take 5 Urdu sentences about your day. Say each in English (record), then translate your English back into Urdu. Where the round trip breaks, that is your transfer point — note it.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. ## Module 2 — Accuracy. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Explain present perfect to a shopkeeper
prompt:
Goal: If you can teach it simply, you own it.

Record 90 seconds explaining present perfect ("I have done") to someone who never studied grammar. Use only examples from your own life. No grammar terms allowed except the tense name.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The -s hunt
prompt:
Goal: Train self-monitoring for 3rd-person -s.

Record 60 seconds about what your friend does every day (he/she sentences). Transcribe it yourself, circle every 3rd-person verb, fix the missing -s endings, then re-record clean.
tip: Lens trained: Structure.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Preposition picture
prompt:
Goal: Use 5 prepositions correctly under light pressure.

Pick any photo on your phone. Describe it in 60 seconds using at least 5 of: in, on, at, behind, next to, between, since, for. Record.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Experience in present perfect (writing)
prompt:
Goal: Portfolio-ready sentences about your real experience.

Write 6 lines about your skills/projects. Use present perfect ("I have built…") at least 3 times. Every claim must be true.
tip: Lens trained: Client-safety. ## Module 3 — Pronunciation. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Shadow a 2-minute clip
prompt:
Goal: 10 minutes of rhythm and stress training.

Pick a 2-minute BBC Learning English clip. Shadow it (speak along, half a second behind) for 10 minutes at 0.75× speed if needed. Record the last 2 minutes.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Minimal-pair drill: thin/tin
prompt:
Goal: Separate /th/ from /t/ by feel.

Record yourself saying thin–tin, thigh–tie, though–dough, 10 rounds. Tongue between teeth for the th words. Listen back — mark any round where they sounded the same.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The thank-you sentence
prompt:
Goal: th-sounds in a real client sentence.

Record 5 clean takes of: "I think this is the best thing for the project, and I thank you for your thoughts." All th-words with tongue between teeth.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Clap the stress
prompt:
Goal: First-syllable stress as a physical habit.

Record 10 words, clapping on the stressed syllable: PHOtograph, COMputer, DEveloper, IMportant, CLIent, PROject, DElivery, TIme-line, UPdate, REport.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The v/w mirror drill
prompt:
Goal: Kill the v/w merger.

In front of a mirror, record: vest–west, vine–wine, very–wary ×5. Teeth on lip = /v/, rounded lips = /w/. Watch your mouth, not just listen.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. ## Module 4 — Fluency. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: 60-second day retell (no stopping)
prompt:
Goal: Continuous speech with zero self-correction.

Record 60 seconds on "what I did today". Rules: no pausing to fix, no restarting, fillers allowed this once. Fluency first.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Same story, smoother (task repetition)
prompt:
Goal: Feel repetition layering accuracy onto fluency.

Take Card 14's recording. Listen once. Re-record the same content — smoother, fewer fillers, fixed verbs. Compare the two takes yourself first.
tip: Lens trained: Structure.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Picture sprint (SVO only)
prompt:
Goal: Automatic sentence building under time pressure.

Open any busy photo. 60 seconds: describe it in SVO sentences only, as many as you can. Count your sentences after.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Filler detox
prompt:
Goal: Zero um/like/you-know for 90 seconds.

Record 90 seconds on "my goals for this year". Count your fillers. Redo it with zero fillers — pause silently instead.
tip: Lens trained: Tone. ## Module 5 — Client Communication. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The 2-day delay email (writing)
prompt:
Goal: The most-sent email in freelancing, done right.

Write a 4–6 line delay email: you need 2 more days on a dashboard. Early warning + honest reason + what you are doing now + new date. Plus a subject line.
tip: Lens trained: Structure + Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Role-play: "too expensive" (speaking)
prompt:
Goal: Handle the #1 price objection out loud without freezing.

Record both sides, 90 seconds: you are the client saying "Too expensive." Then you are yourself, answering. Diagnose before discounting — offer scope options.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Discovery-call opening
prompt:
Goal: Sound in control in the first 60 seconds of a call.

Record your opening: greet, one line about you, then the question that hands them the floor ("Tell me what you are trying to build."). Warm, unhurried.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: "This isn't what I asked for" (writing + speaking)
prompt:
Goal: De-escalate a revision complaint in writing, then voice.

First write your reply (3–4 lines): apologize once, ask for specifics, promise speed. Then read it aloud and record — it must sound calm, not defensive.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: "Why should I hire you?" (speaking)
prompt:
Goal: A 60-second answer with proof, not adjectives.

Record: one similar thing you have built + how you work (milestones, updates) + a low-risk offer (small first milestone). No "hardworking", no "trust me".
tip: Lens trained: Client-safety. ## Module 6 — Self-Presentation & Branding. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: 30 seconds, then 90
prompt:
Goal: An intro that scales to the time you are given.

Record your 30-second intro (name + what you do + one proof). Then record the 90-second version (add how you work + what you want next).
tip: Lens trained: Structure.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Camera answer: "Tell me about yourself"
prompt:
Goal: Survive video-call pressure: eye contact, pacing, no fillers.

Phone on a table, camera on. Answer "Tell me about yourself" in 60 seconds, looking at the lens. Watch it back once — note one thing to fix — then record once more.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Your bio, written and spoken (writing)
prompt:
Goal: A 150-word profile bio that is honest and hireable.

Write a 150-word bio for Upwork/Fiverr: who you are, what you do best, how you work, one honest proof point. Then read it aloud and record — bios get read on calls too.
tip: Lens trained: Client-safety.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Small-talk ladder
prompt:
Goal: Five warm answers, zero awkward silence.

Record answers (20–30 seconds each) to: "How's your day going?" / "Where are you based?" / "How long have you done this?" / "What do you do for fun?" / then pivot: "Tell me about the project."
tip: Lens trained: Tone. ## Module 7 — Sales. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The 60-second proposal pitch
prompt:
Goal: Sell a dashboard project out loud, like a voice note to a client.

Record a 60-second pitch: name their goal back to them, your approach in 2 steps, price with scope, and a start date. End with a question.
tip: Lens trained: Structure.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Follow-up to a quiet client (writing)
prompt:
Goal: One nudge that reopens a stalled proposal.

A client went quiet 3 days after your proposal. Write the follow-up: 3 lines max. Warm, no guilt, offer an adjustment.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Ask for the advance, out loud
prompt:
Goal: Make money talk feel normal, not awkward.

Record 3 versions of asking for a 30% advance. Different words each time. Pick the warmest, mark it, and tell me why it wins.
tip: Lens trained: Tone.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The trial close
prompt:
Goal: End a sales conversation with a clear yes/no question.

Record: "Does that scope and timeline work for you? If yes, I can start tomorrow." Then add your own one-line version. Both must sound confident — voice falling at the end, not rising.
tip: Lens trained: Tone + Client-safety. --- Done all 30? That is a complete output portfolio: 30 recordings + writings, every lens trained, and a before/after trail from Card 1 to Card 30. Keep them — in month 3 you will compare Card 1 against a fresh intro and hear exactly how far you came.. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The 20 openers, aloud
prompt:
Goal: Make small-talk openers automatic.

Read all 20 starter lines from Lesson 8.1 aloud — standing up, smiling, like you mean them. Then pick your 5 favourites and say each one twice more.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Airport arrival narration
prompt:
Goal: Narrate a full arrival without a script.

Record yourself landing in a new country: immigration answers (purpose, duration, hotel), then the hotel check-in script. Full sentences, calm pace — like it's really happening.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The phone recovery drill
prompt:
Goal: Survive a call with zero visual cues.

Call the hotel (AI tutor or voice memo): confirm booking for the 14th — date, room type, price. You MUST use two recovery phrases (repeat / spell / slow down) and one confirm-back ("So that's... correct?").
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Your emergency card
prompt:
Goal: Emergency lines on paper before you need them.

Write: (1) your lost-passport sentence for the police + embassy, (2) your symptom list (8 words from Lesson 8.4), (3) "I'm allergic to penicillin." in your own handwriting — then say it aloud 5 times. Save a passport photo on your phone today.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Three meeting moves
prompt:
Goal: Participate in a meeting without freezing.

AI tutor runs a short meeting. Use all three moves once: agree-and-add, one polite interruption ("Sorry, can I jump in for a second?"), one clarification question. Under 20 seconds per turn.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: The 2-minute presentation
prompt:
Goal: Present a real project with structure.

Deliver 2 minutes on a REAL project of yours: one hook (question, number, or story) → 3 signposted points ("First... Second... Finally...") → one-sentence close + "Happy to take questions." Record and redo once, slower.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: Interview kit aloud
prompt:
Goal: Walk into interviews with the kit loaded.

Speak your 60-second "tell me about yourself" (Present → Past → Future), then one full STAR story with a number in it. Then say your 3 questions to ask them. Real facts only — honesty contract applies double here.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

title: SBI feedback letter
prompt:
Goal: Give feedback that fixes, not fights.

Write SBI+R feedback for a real or imagined situation: Situation, Behavior (fact, not verdict), Impact, Request. Then write the receiving script: "Thanks for telling me — can you give me one example? I'll think about it." Say both aloud.
tip: Lens trained: Clarity. Submit per the feedback contract: tell Muse the task number.

prompt:
Goal: Beat the Listening traps — distractors, paraphrase, signposts.

Re-read the Mock A listening script (Lesson 9). Predict the answer type for each of the 6 questions BEFORE re-reading the answers (number? name? place?). Then have a friend (or your AI tutor) read the script aloud once while you take notes. Score: how many of 6 did you get? Tell Muse the task number and your score.
tip: Prediction first, listening second — that's the whole technique.
title: Trap-hunting: listening under pressure

checklist: Clear position in intro and conclusion
prompt:
Goal: Write a full Task 2 essay in 40 minutes, exam conditions.

Prompt: "Some people believe that social media has improved communication between people. Others think it has made communication worse. Discuss both views and give your own opinion."

Timer on: 40 minutes, 250+ words, no AI help while writing. Then self-score with the Writing rubric (Lesson 6) — one honest "no" = one band lost. Tell Muse the task number and paste the essay for feedback.
tip: Plan 5 minutes, write 30, check 5. The plan is where Band 7 is won.
title: Task 2 essay — full exam conditions

checklist: Caught the NOT GIVEN traps (didn't upgrade guesses)
prompt:
Goal: Run a full Reading passage in 20 minutes.

Take any IELTS Reading passage (or re-do the Mock B passage from Lesson 10 with fresh eyes). Skim 90 seconds for structure, then scan for each answer — no top-to-bottom reading. Timer: 20 minutes hard stop. Any question eating 2+ minutes gets a guess and you move on. Tell Muse the task number and your score out of 8.
tip: The 20-minute rule is non-negotiable: guess and move.
title: Reading sprint — 20 minutes, no mercy

prompt:
Goal: Deliver a complete Part 2 cue-card answer — 1 minute prep, 2 full minutes of speaking.

Topic: "Describe a skill you would like to learn." Structure: past → description → feeling. Then answer 3 Part 3 questions about learning with balanced views. Record it, score it with the Speaking rubric (Lesson 7), re-record the weakest 60 seconds. Tell Muse the task number for feedback.
tip: The silence after you finish early is the examiner waiting — keep talking.
title: Cue-card full talk + Part 3
